name: quest-ai-runner library
description: A domain-free Python library: a bounded plan, gather, re-plan, answer loop that escalates to a deep runner when real work is needed (the core), a task executor that polls Quest, claims, runs, escalates and reports (the runner), and reference adapters for retrieval, model providers, cards, vectors, web research and deep runners, all wired by one configuration per lane and each swappable part chosen by metric.
advantages: One engine for chat and scheduled work; grounded in the consumer's sources; escalation built in; open source and reusable outside Quest; every part measured and swappable.
disadvantages: A large codebase to maintain; chat answer quality is currently weak on the cheapest model; some parts are measured only offline; consumers must keep adapters in step with the library.

name: Prefix-routing multi-provider
description: Wraps a primary provider and a set of vendor providers, routes each call by model-name prefix, steps down a tier when a quota error occurs, and applies shared retry for transient errors. Callers see one provider.
advantages: Vendor and tier changes are configuration, and quota exhaustion degrades service instead of failing. It beats a single flat provider on the offline cases. Selected because: QAR_MODEL_BACKEND and ModelRegistry tiers
disadvantages: More moving parts and a per-call routing decision. Fallback hides a degraded tier unless logged, and price knowledge is input-only.

name: Digest-driven overseer
description: Builds a capped compact digest of the run, makes one structured model call with a fixed prompt and tool schema, validates the answer against the five signals, and returns proceed on any error, non-object response or unknown signal.
advantages: Very low token cost, safe by default, and cannot distort a run without an explicit signal. Selected because: RunnerConfig.overseer
disadvantages: Quality rests on the digest keeping the right evidence and on a model deciding well, and the live signal match is unmeasured.

name: Offline lifecycle harness
description: Runs the real poller, executor, persona resolver, folder sync, scheduling helper and lane helpers against a fake client and a scripted model, with no model calls.
advantages: Deterministic and free coverage of the whole lifecycle including duplicates, lost claims and team scoping. Selected because: runner/config_wiring.py (a lane's run_lane drives Poller and TaskExecutor)
disadvantages: The fake client hides wire-level behaviour such as HTTP errors and real payload shapes, and crash recovery of orphaned claims is not yet covered.

name: Static price table lookup
description: Holds a snapshot of list prices per million input tokens by provider and model, detects the provider from the environment, falls back to a stated default for unknown models, and estimates bootstrap cost from a token count.
advantages: Simple, offline and instant, and gives a cost estimate before any spend.
disadvantages: Hand-maintained, input tokens only, and stale until someone edits it.

name: Persisted daily token tracker
description: Counts input and output tokens within a UTC day, persists the tally to a JSON file so a restart reloads it, resets at the day boundary, and reports over-limit and a status line. A limit of zero or off disables it.
advantages: Survives restarts and cleanly separates days; opt-in so it never surprises a lane.
disadvantages: Counts tokens, not money, and a deep runner on a subscription is outside the count; a lost usage file resets the day.

name: Hysteresis resource guard
description: Samples memory use, free memory and load, pauses new work when a limit is exceeded and resumes only after readings clear, and can wait until the host is fine. Sampling uses the process file system or a library, with limits from code or the environment.
advantages: Hysteresis prevents flapping, and pausing is lossless because unclaimed work stays queued.
disadvantages: Thresholds are manual and host-specific, and the sampler depends on platform facilities that may be absent.

name: Apply the evolvable-structure library
description: QAR keeps its specifications as records under esoi and builds on the library's solutions to apply a project's structure: the application procedure, the structure check, the measurement harness and the implementation selector.
advantages: No checker of QAR's own to maintain; every part is compared on the same cases and selected by its metric. Selected because: the evolvable-structure library already carries the machinery; QAR keeps only its records and configuration
disadvantages: A dependency pinned by commit, and a runtime one because implementations are declared with its decorators; a rule or format change in the library needs a migration here; offline arms only unless a paid arm is run by decision.

name: Rebuilt prompt per step with a referenced context (today)
description: Each step is a fresh planner call built from the template, the cached head and context layers, the newest observations in full and older ones in one line; from the second step the transcript and the context block are replaced by a short note that refers to step one.
advantages: Built and selected; the smallest planner input per step; the final answer still sees everything.
disadvantages: From the second step the planner sees neither the transcript nor the context block, and is told it saw them; continuity across steps is unmeasured.

name: Web research with the answer's support check (today)
description: World questions are answered from the model's knowledge and snippet-first web research, and the answer check flags claims the turn's reads do not support and rewrites them once with their basis.
advantages: Built; cheap and fast; unsupported claims are hedged rather than asserted.
disadvantages: No evidence-strength label; a host's research sources are not consulted unless wired as a retrieval source or a tool; general knowledge that passes the check is still stated without a source.

name: Managed quest card plus optional live reads (today)
description: A managed card per quest, rebuilt when the quest syncs, grounds each turn, and the planner issues live reads through the host's retrieval adapter when it wants more.
advantages: Built; cheap; one card per quest that every surface shares.
disadvantages: The card lags changes made since the last sync, including the AI's own; reads are optional; nothing is read back after a change, so two answers in a session can rest on different reads.

name: Separate stores read at the start of a request (today)
description: Conversation recall, recent context, feedback guidance, predictions, reflections and quest cards are each read separately at the start of a request and prepended to the context block, fenced per quest or global; a representative's learned notes and context preferences are read with no scope; declined proposals arrive from the host's escalation history.
advantages: Built; each store is measured on its own; a failure in one does not stop the others.
disadvantages: No view of what an intent or the quest settled; several budgets and paths, each of which must apply the fence; the representative's notes cross quests; chat and background work read different subsets.

name: Code-enforced before and after on deep runs only (today)
description: Around every deep goal the slice is found, the metric is read before and after by the runner's meters, rows go to the ledger, and a changed run with nothing on record is asked once and otherwise marked missing; chat turns and in-process work are not covered.
advantages: Built and shown in the terminal and the host's chat; decided from the ledger, never from words.
disadvantages: Covers only deep runs; nothing acts on a regression or a missing metric; no metric is proposed when none applies.

name: Channels, terminal and package as ways in
description: Each way in is its own measured solution, and every one hands its request to the same router. The package's front door is taught by its documents (explain-qar), shown by its examples (learn-by-example) and set up through one layered configuration (configure-a-lane).
advantages: A new channel is one more solution beneath this one, measured on its own.
disadvantages: No metric judges the ways in together; only each one's own.

name: Quest HTTP client from the environment
description: Builds the Quest client from QUEST_BASE_URL (or QUEST_API_URL), QUEST_API_KEY and, when set, QUEST_TEAM_ID, so the runner works in the account those name.
advantages: One client for every consumer of the runner; nothing to pass when the environment is set.
disadvantages: Reads one account; a deployment that serves several teams passes its own client.
